maya: Quick summary of the last 72h infer runs comparing Ampere (A100) vs Hopper (H100) across regions. Ran 7B and 13B, int8 and fp16, batch sizes 1/8/32, seq 512/1024. results pasted below.

sam: nice — did you capture both 'context load' and 'token gen' phases separately?

maya: yep. we split into: context_load (first-token latency to populate KV), and steady_token_rate (tokens/sec). gave cost extrapolation to $/1M tokens using our on-demand price sheet.

kevin: curious about kernels used — did you force flash or let runtime pick?

maya: let runtime pick on prod images but also ran toggles. key variants: flash_attn2 on H100, cutlass+triton on A100, and a fallback path that uses slower aten kernels for small seqs. noted when kernel fallthrough happened.

ops-bot: Deploy-run completed: bench-run/2189554321 finished — artifacts:/runs/2189554321/*

maya: here's the short CSV I pasted from the logs (columns: model,quant,device,region,ctx_ms, tok_s, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1M_usd, notes)
```
model,quant,device,region,ctx_ms,tok_s,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1M_usd,notes
redwood-7b,int8,H100,us-west-2,58,120,12000,0.39,flash_attn2 active
redwood-7b,int8,A100,us-west-2,95,76,7600,0.62,cutlass+triton
redwood-7b,fp16,H100,eu-central-1,62,110,11000,0.47,slightly higher ctx in eu
redwood-7b,int4,A100,eu-central-1,110,50,5000,0.95,quantization regressed gen quality
redwood-13b,fp16,H100,us-west-2,120,58,5800,0.82,good stability
redwood-13b,int8,A100,us-west-2,210,34,3400,1.40,large ctx load; kernel fallthroughs
```

maya: highlights: H100 int8 gives ~1.5x-1.6x tokens/sec vs A100 int8 for 7B in same region. context load (first-token) is ~40-90ms faster on H100 for these sizes.

kevin: those int4 A100 numbers look rough — you saw quality drop? eval BLEU/perplex changes?

maya: yes, int4 produced a measurable perplexity increase on our small eval set (median +12%). we flagged it as a regression. keeping int4 for 7B only in offline batch tests, not for hosted low-latency routes.

sam: region delta: eu-central ctx_ms + ~5-15ms vs us-west for same HW? network or kernel scheduling?

maya: mostly instance flavor differences + slightly older microcode in eu rack. not network — KV load is compute-bound. we saw more cutlass fallbacks in eu A100 runs which added ~20-40ms.

leo: for capacity sizing — if a customer needs 2000 qps steady with avg response 80 tokens, what are rough GPU counts per device?

maya: quick calc: tokens/sec per GPU (7B int8): H100 ~12k, A100 ~7.6k. For 2000 qps * 80 tokens = 160k tokens/sec. So H100: ~14 GPUs (160k/12k = 13.3 -> 14), A100: ~21 GPUs. add 20% headroom, H100 -> 17, A100 -> 25.

kevin: cost extrap for 1M tokens in csv uses on-demand hourly; did you include amortized instance overhead (idle, checkpoints)?

maya: we included basic infra overhead (2.3% added to unit costs) and a small I/O amortization. not full ops margin. treat those $/1M as comparative, not billing-ready.

sam: did you capture variance (p95) for token latency? steady-state jitter matters for realtime.

maya: yes — median tok latency / steady token-time reported; p95 token latency for H100 int8 was ~1.8x median under microburst tests, A100 was ~2.3x. microburst=short QPS spike test (10s windows).

ops-bot: Note: bench artifacts include perf flamegraphs and kernel telemetry at /runs/2189554321/telemetry.tar.gz

maya: commands I ran (for reproducibility):
```
# run single config example
redwood-bench --model redwood-7b --device h100 --quant int8 --batch 8 --seq 512 --region us-west-2 --out /runs/2189554321/h100-7b-int8
```

kevin: helpful — any surprising kernel fallbacks to call out?

maya: A100 runs for 13B hit a couple of kernel fallthroughs into aten when seq>1024; that tanked tok/s and spiked ctx_ms. H100 didn't fall through there (flash_attn2 handles >1024). noted that on the run.

sam: recommendation for production routes: for conversational low-latency we recommend H100 + int8 for 7B/13B when quality verified; A100 is OK for batch/cheaper embeddings/throughput-flexible.

maya: add nuance: if cost-per-token is primary and you can accept slightly higher tail latencies, A100 int8 with more batching gives lower $/1M in heavy batch workloads. For interactive apps H100 saves infra headcount and headroom.

leo: any followups we need ops to action? kernel patches to deploy?

maya: filing two tickets: (1) eu A100 microcode upgrade + cutlass runtime bump (ticket #INF-7882) (2) eval suite for int4 quality with larger eval sets (ticket #INF-7883).

kevin: cool. can you also attach small perf matrix with command flags used per run? I'll pull into the model-onboarding doc.

maya: will attach artifacts and a compact table. linking run folder here: /runs/2189554321/summary.md

sam: thanks — this is actionable. :thumbsup:

maya: tl;dr: H100 wins on latency and tokens/sec (~1.5-1.6x vs A100 on our 7B tests), A100 can be cheaper at scale for batch with more batching, int4 still risky for quality in prod, region infra differences caused some kernel fallbacks in eu.
